photos.method: the photograph was first turned 2.6 degrees about (265, 335) because the board's vertical edges ran 2 to 3 degrees off the picture's vertical (the left edge moved 22 px and the right edge 14 px over 420 rows); each edge is the strongest grey-level step inside the recorded window, averaged over the recorded band; the scale is fitted on the one height from the leaf's top edge to the left foot's lower edge (592.3 px) and the width, the right foot, the arch and the centre are predicted from it; the leaf's width of 600 mm is the unit that sets the absolute size (Judgement), so the check is of proportions; the tolerance is the measured spread times 3 plus 2 px, at least 5 px (8 mm); the right foot sits 4.2 px higher than the left in the picture (the ground slopes), inside the tolerance

ratio.note: taken at rows 500 to 520 and columns 505 to 535; the board is sheared about 6 degrees in the picture (its left edge moves 7 px and its right edge 9 px over 65 rows) and tilted back, so only the ratio is used

photos.method: each edge is the strongest grey-level step inside the recorded window, averaged over the recorded band; no scale is fitted (the board's plane is neither square on nor level); only the projected width over the projected height is used, against the same ratio of the AB2 front leaf's drawing

sources.author: Walter Baxter
sources.shows: a painted plywood A-board on a village pavement, front leaf square on: a plain rectangle with two feet and a flared arch cut in its lower edge, painted lettering in black, pink and blue, a bare-ply edge strip on its right side, the back leaf's edge beside it, and a loose steel chain hanging from a screw eye in the right edge
sources.not_used_for: any lettering or name (it names a tea room and carries a hard-hat picture; none is copied), the colours of the lettering, any absolute size (no scale object; the leaf's width is assumed), the lean (a front view)
sources.period: 2013 photograph of a home-made board of a type that was common long before 1990 (ply, hinges, chain, foot arch); it is the construction that is used, never its date

sources.author: Alan Murray-Rust
sources.shows: a framed white notice board leaning against the front of an open-top tour bus on a bus station apron: a thin timber frame holding a white panel with a printed card, standing on the ground at a lean; people and a bus operator's marks are in the picture
sources.not_used_for: the people (not drawn, not in any preview), the operator's name and plates (real marks, masked), the card's wording, the board's absolute size (the bus tyre as a scale is judged to 15 percent)
sources.period: 1978: the only 1975 to 1995 photograph of a pavement board that was found; 12 years before the game but the same trade type

sources.author: HelenK
sources.shows: a green-bordered black chalkboard on an A-frame with an arched top outside a cafe, on a wet pavement beside a road
sources.not_used_for: everything: looked at and set aside; a painted chalk menu board with an arched top is a 2010s fashion that no 1975 to 1995 photograph found here supports, and it is not a fishmonger's board

text.no_name: no shop name on the board and no logo; the fish market is the fish market (hook-cast names: the fish market, the fishmonger's, the market)
text.style: hand-painted signwriter's capitals in black emulsion on the off-white leaf, a plain upright narrow face; letters of uneven height by 2 to 3 percent, not a font on the final mesh (the decal is painted by hand, then ground into the wear)
text.currency: pounds and pence as 2.60 and pence as 95P, the price is per pound (LB) unless EACH
text.faces: both outer faces carry the same list (the board's two faces look up and down the pavement), the back leaf's lines identical

lines.basis: invented: a little under cod; no 1990 figure was found

text.ab2_note: AB2 carries a notice card of 400 x 640 whose wording is a decal chosen by the street (never this target); no shop name

night.note: the board is not out at night: the fish market shuts at 14.00 (13.00 on Wednesdays) and the board goes indoors; in a dusk shot it stands in the dark between lamp pools (the nearest lamp column is x 8 east, 6 m away) and its off-white face takes the lantern colour only as a faint wash on the face turned towards the lamp

placement.slot: east pavement outside the fish market (bay 1, x 9 to 15): centre x 14.45 m, centre z 4.600 m (1.60 m from the kerb face), the board's two faces looking up and down the pavement (the scene's yaw 90), its back leaf's feet 0.063 m clear of the stallriser line; it replaces the scene's line at x 15.2, 1.1 m from the kerb face
reasons: the scene's line stood at x 15.2 with its 0.68 m width across the pavement and its centre 1.1 m from the kerb face: it left 0.64 m on the kerb side and 0.54 m on the shop side of a 1.85 m footway, both under the 0.68 m of a walking person (the 29 September walk found the footway walled by a smaller obstruction), and its depth put it on the line of the party pilaster between the fish market and Rita's
against the stallriser the board leaves 1.16 m clear on the kerb side, over the 1.0 m this target requires; the board is a shopkeeper's, put where the pavement is widest beside the shop

x 14.45 is in front of the fish market's own window (bay 1 is x 9 to 15, RULINGS 3 Oct) and clear of Rita's (the pilaster face is 0.157 m beyond the board's end); the awning (x 10.5 to 13.5) is 0.73 m away and the pavement spot where the cast stands (x 12.0, z 4.2) is 2.5 m away, so nobody who waits at the fish market stands behind the board
the fish market's doorway is at about x 9.4 and the board stands 5 m from it, so no door is blocked; the railing by the gully (x 10 to 12) is 2.2 m away
the faces look along the pavement, as the scene had them: a board read by people walking up or down the street; the leaf's long side lies across the pavement
the board is out only in the market's hours (Monday to Saturday from 7.30, shut at 14.00, Wednesday 13.00); a night frame has no board

wear: the leaf's paint is chalking off-white with a grey splash band to 150 mm above the paving, the lower arris and the feet's edges worn to bare ply; the top edge and the right arris carry rust-brown weeping from the glue line (P1)
lettering is hand-painted and slightly uneven; one letter is overpainted in a second colour (P1 shows a word corrected in blue): a decal detail, not a mesh one
the feet's arch is dirty to its flared edges; the ply swells at the foot's corners (a 2 mm lift) and the lower 40 mm of the bare edge is dark
the screw eyes are grey with a rust ring; the chain is dull, two links rusted, hanging in a deep loop between the leaves (P1)
the back of each leaf is bare grey-brown batten and ply, never painted

variants_note: AB1 (the sample): the fish market's painted board, one outside the fish market, out in its hours (7.30 to 14.00, Wednesday 13.00).

AB2: the smaller framed notice board of S2's type (508 x 762, thin frame, white panel, a notice card); for the newsagent or the tea room if the town wants one; not placed today. The newsagent's wire-fronted headline board of the asset plan is a different object (its paper's name is owed by canon) and is not written here.
conditions (materials): C0 sound; C1 worn (the sample's wear); C2 a leaf with a corner chipped to bare ply and the chain missing (a seed, not a mesh).
lettering: T1 the fish list as written; T2 the same list with one price overpainted (a decal mask over T1, never other words).
not_settled: absolute sizes: S1 has no scale object, the leaf's width (600 mm) is assumed and sets 0.612 px per mm; every size from S1 is Judgement or Photo within the stated error; AB2's size rests on S2's tyre as a scale, good to about 15 percent
the lean (12 degrees): neither photograph is a side view; a real board stands between 10 and 15 degrees

the 1975 to 1995 date of S1's type: the only dated photograph (S2, 1978) shows a framed board, not a painted ply board with a foot arch; a home-made painted board is certainly older than 1990, but no 1990 photograph of one was found
the hinges and the back battens: both are hidden from the front and no photograph shows them (Judgement)
the other fish's 1990 prices (only the cod's is sourced); and the wording a real fishmonger would have painted
whether Quay Street's fishmonger put the board out every day (the hours say when it could be out; the town has no rule)
content_rule_note: no shop name, advertisement, person, drink or betting wording on any face (a statement of the content rule).
builder_notes: leaf: a 12 mm ply panel 600 wide from the arch's top to the ridge plus two feet cut with the flared arch, all one mesh of one material; the arch's flared sides are the polygon in the foot parts; the painted face is the decal (text.lines) laid on the outer face, 3 px per mm

pose: both leaves hang from the ridge line (the pivot in each part's xf) and lean 12 degrees, the front leaf's face looking -y; the lowest edge of each leaf is its inner foot edge on the paving; build in the leaf's own frame and use the xf as given
the chain: 16 straight 5 mm segments along the catenary in the wire part (a chain of links is a texture on a tube); it hangs free of both leaves and of the ground (its lowest point is 350 mm up)
hinges: two butt hinges on the inner faces, knuckles on the ridge line; the leaves' top inner edges meet there
orientation: the local -y faces up the pavement for the front leaf; the street's yaw 90 turns the board so the two faces look along the pavement
